title: dispatch makes one worktree per required repository from its fetched default branch
goal: dispatch makes, for each repository of the item's repos, a worktree at <worktree_dir>/<id>/<repo> branched from that repository's fetched origin default branch (a repository of repos_if_needed only when the worker asks: none by default); a repository whose fetch fails refuses the dispatch naming it; with no repositories map dispatch makes the one worktree as today

gates.question: Where does a repository's worktree go under the configured worktree directory?
options: <worktree_dir>/<id>/<repo>: one directory per item, one subdirectory per repository
gates.recommendation: <worktree_dir>/<id>/<repo>: one directory per item, one subdirectory per repository
gates.answer: <worktree_dir>/<id>/<repo>: one directory per item, one subdirectory per repository

gates.question: Does dispatch make a worktree for a repository of repos_if_needed?
options: no: only the required repositories, and the worker asks for another when it needs it
yes: every repository of repos_if_needed too
gates.recommendation: no: only the required repositories, and the worker asks for another when it needs it
gates.answer: no: only the required repositories, and the worker asks for another when it needs it

gates.question: In a workspace with a repositories map, does dispatch still make the workspace's own worktree agent-<id> beside the repository worktrees?
options: yes: the workspace worktree is made as today (the worker's working directory, role file, _tools and item file live there) and each required repository gets one more at <worktree_dir>/<id>/<repo>
no: only the repository worktrees exist and the worker has no workspace worktree
gates.recommendation: yes: the workspace worktree is made as today (the worker's working directory, role file, _tools and item file live there) and each required repository gets one more at <worktree_dir>/<id>/<repo>

gates.question: Does a repository's worktree made by dispatch track the repository's origin default branch as its upstream?
options: no: --no-track, no upstream, as the workspace's own worktree has none
yes: git's default for a remote-tracking start point, upstream origin/<default>
gates.recommendation: no: --no-track, no upstream, as the workspace's own worktree has none
